textPreview: Global-slot WHNO reached 2-D RMSE 0.1453. |  | Changing where the transform acts mattered more than changing the local branch itself.

text:
Timing: 1:00

Describe neural operators as learnable integral/convolutional maps. The first move was FNO. Wavelets and Walsh–Hadamard then changed the representation. The surprising empirical lesson was architectural: the global bottleneck benefited most from the non-Fourier transform.

text: k → Rφ(k): generate the spectral kernel over the full grid instead of storing a truncated mode table.
textPreview: k → Rφ(k): generate the spectral kernel over the full grid instead of storing a truncated mode table.

text:
Timing: 1:05

This is the synthesis. U-FNO supplied the local convolutional path; the Local-FNO introduced explicit windowed/local and whole-field/global slots; SirenFNO replaced per-mode tables with an implicit full-frequency kernel. Keeping the slots swappable made the experiments controlled rather than anecdotal.

alt: Representative L2 prediction showing softened ionization bubble boundaries
Representative exponential wall-distance prediction showing sharper bubble boundaries

text:
Timing: 1:15

This is the central tradeoff. L2 prefers a conditional mean when the wall position is uncertain, so it hedges with a ramp. Exponential wall-weighted absolute error instead selects a side. It recovers truth-like width and much more high-k power, but the field RMSE rises by about twenty-two percent.

text:
Timing: 0:55

RMSE does not ask whether the bubble population is physically right. The U-FNO recovers the distribution shape well, with small JS divergence, but the characteristic size is biased by several percent and peaks near nine percent in one stage bin. That is a physically meaningful error for power spectra and EFT-scale interpretation.
